statement_en: Show that there are infinitely many integers m ≥ 2 such that every prime factor q of m satisfies q² < m and every prime factor q of m + 1 satisfies q² < m + 1.
statement_lean:
theorem erdos_52603 :
    Set.Infinite {m : ℕ | 2 ≤ m ∧ (∀ q ∈ m.primeFactors, q ^ 2 < m) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ (m + 1).primeFactors, q ^ 2 < m + 1)} := by
  sorry
changes: alpha-renaming only: n→m, p→q; theorem renamed to a synthetic id; English paraphrased without 'largest prime factor', 'smooth' or attribution; tags removed
